title: Euler liar probability over repeated rounds
statement: Let $N>1$ be an odd composite natural number, and let $\ell,k$ be natural numbers. In each of $k$ rounds, use a block of $\ell$ uniformly random bits to form a candidate by interpreting the block as a binary integer, reducing it modulo $N-1$, and adding $1$; the rounds accept when every candidate is an Euler liar to base $N$. The probability of acceptance using $\ell k$ uniformly random bits is at most $\left(\frac12+\frac{N-1}{2^{\ell+1}}\right)^k$.
